title: Kundu (hand drum)
summary: The kundu is a tall hand drum of Papua New Guinea, carved from a single piece of wood with a narrow waist, a grip at the middle and an open foot. A stretched hide covers the top and a lump of black paste tunes it; the body is cut with bands of triangles and chevrons painted in ochre, white and black.
howToPlay: The drum stands upright: the hide on top, the carved grip at the waist and the open foot at the bottom.
Centre is the middle of the hide and Edge the ring round it. Grip is a knock on the carved waist and Mouth a deep stroke over the open foot.
A ring closes on the place to strike. Strike as it lands.
Begin with the centre strokes, then add the edge and the grip.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The patterns count four beats to the bar.
heritageNote: Kundu drums are carved and tuned by their players, and the patterns cut into the wood often belong to a family or a place. The drum is held by its grip and played for dances and songs, its pitch set by the paste on the hide.
credits: Tradition: the Kundu; patterns written for this game
